title: India on the Eve of British Conquest

faqs.q: During whose reign is the beginning of the end of Mughal rule generally considered to have started?
faqs.e: Aurangzeb reigned from 1658 to 1707.

faqs.q: For how many years did Muhammad Shah rule?
faqs.e: He ruled from 1719 to 1748 but was an incompetent ruler who could not revive imperial fortunes.

faqs.q: Which Persian emperor attacked India in 1738-39 and defeated the Mughal army at Karnal?
On which date was the Mughal army defeated at Karnal by Nadir Shah?
Apart from the Peacock Throne and the Kohinoor diamond, how much money is estimated to have been collected by Nadir Shah from the official treasury and nobles' safes?
Ahmad Shah Abdali was elected successor to Nadir Shah after the latter's death in which year?
Which Rohilla chief did Ahmad Shah Abdali recognise as Mir Bakhshi of the empire and his personal 'supreme agent' in 1757?
Which Maratha chief expelled Najib-ud-Daula from Delhi and captured Punjab in 1758?
In which year did Ahmad Shah Abdali defeat the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat?

Consider the following statements regarding the Battles of Panipat:
(I) The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi.
(II) The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar and Hemu.
(III) The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Who became Mughal emperor after a nearly two-year war of succession, taking the title Bahadur Shah I?
faqs.e: He was the eldest son of Aurangzeb and had killed his brothers Muhammad Azam and Kam Bakhsh in the war of succession.

faqs.q: Which title did the historian Khafi Khan give to Bahadur Shah I?

Who introduced the izara system to improve the empire's financial condition during the reign of Jahandar Shah?
Farrukhsiyar became emperor after killing Jahandar Shah with the help of the 'King Makers', known as the:
faqs.e: The Sayyid brothers were Abdulla Khan and Hussain Ali.

faqs.q: In 1717, Farrukhsiyar gave farmans to which power, later regarded as the 'Magna Carta' of that power's trading rights?
Who was dethroned, blinded and killed by the Sayyid brothers in 1719, with the help of Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath?
faqs.e: This was the first time in Mughal history that an emperor was killed by his own nobles.

faqs.q: Which Mughal ruler had the shortest reign in Mughal history?
faqs.e: He ruled only from February 28 to June 4, 1719.

faqs.q: Which emperor was given the title 'Rangeela' due to his luxurious lifestyle?
faqs.e: He was originally named Raushan Akhtar.

faqs.q: With whose help did Muhammad Shah kill the Sayyid Brothers?
faqs.e: In 1724, Nizam-ul-Mulk became wazir and founded the independent state of Hyderabad.

faqs.q: During whose reign was the Battle of Plassey fought in June 1757?
By the Treaty of Allahabad (August 1765), which Mughal emperor granted the East India Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa?
faqs.e: His reign also saw the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) and the Battle of Buxar (1764).

faqs.q: Who gave the title of Raja to Rammohan Rai?
faqs.e: In 1835, coins bearing the names of Mughal emperors were also stopped.

faqs.q: Who was the last Mughal emperor?
faqs.e: Also known as Bahadur Shah Zafar, he was captured by the English after the Revolt of 1857 and died in exile in Rangoon in 1862.

faqs.q: On which date did the Mughal Empire legally come to an end with the declaration of Queen Victoria?
Which class of hereditary landowners, also known as rais, rajas, thakurs, khuts or deshmukhs, helped in revenue collection and local administration under the Mughals?

Consider the following statements regarding causes of the Mughal Empire's decline:
(I) The absence of a definite law of succession fostered wars of succession and partisanship.
(II) Aurangzeb's Deccan policy kept the emperor away from the capital for a long duration.
(III) The invasions of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali gave a death-blow to the empire.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Who founded the Asaf-Jah house of Hyderabad?
In which battle did Nizam-ul-Mulk defeat and kill Mubariz Khan to gain control of the Deccan?
faqs.e: This battle took place in 1724; Nizam-ul-Mulk conferred on himself the title of Asaf-Jah in 1725.

faqs.q: Who was the founder of the independent principality of Awadh, popularly known as Burhan-ul-Mulk?
Who was the founder of the independent state of Bengal?
Alivardi Khan, the deputy governor of Bihar, killed which Bengal ruler at Gheria in 1740 to seize power?
Which Mughal ruler marched against Ajit Singh of the Rajputs in 1708, breaking his alliance with Jai Singh II and Durgadas Rathor?
Which dynasty ruled Mysore before it was brought under Haider Ali's control?
Who established the independent state of Kerala with Travancore as its capital?
faqs.e: He extended his state's boundaries from Kanyakumari to Cochin and organised his army along the Western model.

faqs.q: Under which ruler did the Jat power at Bharatpur reach its zenith?
faqs.e: His state extended from the Ganga in the east to the Chambal in the south, including the subahs of Agra, Mathura, Meerut and Aligarh.

faqs.q: In which year did Suraj Mal die, after which the Jat state declined?
Who assumed leadership of the Sikhs in 1708 but was later defeated and killed?
How many misls or confederacies did the Sikhs organise themselves into following the invasions of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali?
Ranjit Singh, the founder of the Sikh kingdom of Punjab, was the son of the leader of which misl?
faqs.e: His father was Mahan Singh.

faqs.q: Ranjit Singh conquered Lahore and Amritsar in which respective years?

In 1838, Ranjit Singh signed the Tripartite Treaty with the English Company and which ruler, agreeing to provide passage for British troops through Punjab?
faqs.e: The purpose was to place Shah Shuja on the throne of Kabul.

faqs.q: Which Afghan set up an independent kingdom around Farrukhabad during the reigns of Farrukhsiyar and Muhammad Shah?
Who took advantage of the collapse of authority following Nadir Shah's invasion to set up the kingdom of Rohilakhand?
What was the general condition of Indian agriculture in the 18th century despite peasants' hard labour?
faqs.e: Peasants were forced to pay exorbitant amounts to the state, zamindars, jagirdars and revenue-farmers.

faqs.q: Since India was largely self-sufficient in handicrafts and agricultural products in the 18th century, how was its trade balance generally described?

options.c: Exports exceeded imports, balanced by import of silver and gold
options.d: Trade was banned by regional rulers

faqs.a: Exports exceeded imports, balanced by import of silver and gold
faqs.e: India was known as a "sink of precious metals."

faqs.q: From which region did India import pearls, raw silk, wool, dates, dried fruits, and rose water?
Which item was NOT among India's major exports in the 18th century?
faqs.e: Woollen cloth was imported from Europe and Tibet, whereas cotton textiles, indigo and saltpetre were major Indian exports.

faqs.q: Which region was noted as a centre of woollen manufactures in 18th century India?
Which regions were the leaders in India's ship-building industry?

options.d: Maharashtra, the Andhra region and Bengal

faqs.a: Maharashtra, the Andhra region and Bengal
faqs.e: Indian shipping also flourished on the Kerala coast at Calicut and Quilon.

faqs.q: Whose navy put up a good defence on the west coast against the Portuguese?

(I) Upper class women generally remained at home, while lower class women worked in fields.
(II) Practices such as purdah, sati, child marriage and polygamy hindered women's progress.
(III) In most social groups except in Kerala, women possessed little individuality of their own.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.d: Rammohan Rai and Sawai Jai Singh

faqs.a: Raja Sawai Jai Singh of Amber and Maratha General Prashuram Bhau

faqs.e: The observatories were built at Delhi, Jaipur, Benares, Mathura and Ujjain; he also prepared astronomical time-tables called Jij Muhammad-shahi.
